headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Roo Code can write and execute in the VS Code workspace while LightZero is unverified and non-isolated, creating dangerous prompt, data, and action-cascade pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code reads and acts on workspace files by default, and its shared-state model is via filesystem; LightZero is a game-playing agent with no documented isolation or provenance controls. That creates a plausible file-based instruction bridge, though not a direct shared channel. The pathway is weaker than high because LightZero has no explicit file I/O capability.
conditions: IF LightZero outputs text into a workspace file that Roo Code later opens
IF Roo Code treats workspace file contents as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces
Disable automatic file ingestion in Roo Code for untrusted folders
Use a read-only mount for any files LightZero can access
Add a manual review step before Roo Code follows file content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for agent-generated files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code can read workspace files, run browsers, and call configured model APIs; LightZero has no declared data classes, but the pair still creates a default workspace leakage path if sensitive files are present. Because LightZero is unverified and its I/O is undocumented, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF sensitive source code or secrets are present in the shared VS Code workspace
IF Roo Code is configured to send workspace content to a third-party model API
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace
Use a separate non-sensitive workspace for Roo Code
Restrict Roo Code model access to a local provider
Rotate any secrets already stored in workspace files
requires-engineering: enforce file-level redaction before API calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and git modification capabilities in the workspace, while LightZero is not runnable and has no write surface. The conflict is one-sided in practice, but Roo Code's default write-and-git powers on a shared workspace are dangerous and can overwrite or race with any files LightZero produces or consumes.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same VS Code workspace directory
IF Roo Code performs git or file writes while LightZero-generated artifacts are present
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable git writes in Roo Code for shared repos
Use branch-per-agent workflows
Pause one agent before the other writes
requires-engineering: add workspace locking across instances

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can act on outputs from other tools and has browser and shell authority, so if it consumes LightZero-generated text as authoritative, errors can cascade into edits or actions. LightZero lacks documented verification or provenance features, making the handoff fragile, but the absence of explicit downstream automation keeps this below high.
conditions: IF LightZero output is copied into Roo Code prompts or files
IF Roo Code executes shell, git, or browser actions based on that output without verification
mitigations: Require human verification before Roo Code acts on LightZero output
Use structured schemas for any handoff between agents
Log and diff all agent-generated claims before execution
Limit Roo Code to read-only review mode for the handoff
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking between agents

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, retention, or regulated-data mismatch is documented for LightZero, while Roo Code handles source code and browser screenshots and may send data to configured model APIs. The compliance risk is therefore limited to ordinary workspace governance rather than a proven regulatory breach, and the other agent is not cited because no compliance surface is declared for it.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace
IF Roo Code is configured to transmit that data to a non-compliant external model provider
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Use a compliant local model endpoint
Review Roo Code retention settings
Separate regulated and non-regulated projects
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
